title: Wet or Dry? Six Creators on Removing Black Sand with a Magnet
question: Should magnetic black sand be removed from fine-gold concentrate while dry or under water?

sampling.method: Purposeful selection of six creators with accessible primary written instructions or newly reviewed automatic captions; not a random sample or complete creator census.
sampling.unit: One creator, counted once; multiple sources do not create additional votes.
sampling.notEstablished: Population prevalence, exclusive wet preference, comparative recovery, or a universal best method.

sources.creator: Chris Ralph
sources.title: Dealing with Black Sands: Capturing the Gold
sources.tableDetail: A magnet above a thin submerged layer; check the removed fraction.
sources.limits: Personal workflow; no matched wet-versus-dry recovery trial.

sources.creator: Dave McCracken
sources.title: Gold Panning Instructions

sources.limits: A described checking routine, not a measured recovery percentage.

sources.limits: Drying the removed fraction for checking is not a dry-feed recommendation.

sources.creator: Dan Hurd
sources.title: How-to use magnets to recover your gold.

sources.limits: Caption-supported account; no independently measured loss or controlled comparison. This source does not establish his position for every later tool.
sources.editorialLimit: Only the early magnetic segment is summarized; later mercury-related context is excluded.

Record magnet placement, tool, classification and loading
Retain magnetic and nonmagnetic fractions with their washings

Compare accounted loss fractions rather than raw tailings amounts
